# Anycode v0.3.3

Anycode v0.3.3 is a patch release fixing `SIGILL` (illegal instruction) crashes at startup in the Linux Desktop build (`anycode-desktop`) on older `x86-64` processors and hypervisors, adding the `anycode update` self-update CLI command, publishing the Desktop auto-updater manifest (`latest.json`), and pinning CI Linux runners to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.

## Desktop & Linux Binary Compatibility

- **x86-64 Baseline for Desktop & All x86_64 Targets**: Enforced baseline `x86-64` instruction generation (`-C target-cpu=x86-64 -C target-feature=-avx,-avx2,-bmi,-bmi2,-fma,-f16c` and `CFLAGS`/`CXXFLAGS` `-march=x86-64 -mtune=generic -mno-avx -mno-avx2 -mno-fma -mno-bmi -mno-bmi2 -mno-f16c`) across Desktop (`anycode-desktop`) and CLI builds. Prevents bundled C dependencies (such as `libsqlite3-sys`) from emitting `FMA3` (`vfmadd213sd`) instructions that crash on pre-Haswell CPUs (e.g. Intel Sandy Bridge / Ivy Bridge) and virtualized environments.
- **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS CI Runners**: Pinned Linux CI and release builds to `ubuntu-24.04` LTS instead of floating `ubuntu-latest` to ensure consistent `glibc` and toolchain baselines across releases.
- **Automated CI ISA Verification**: Added post-build disassembly checks (`objdump -d`) in CI for both CLI and Desktop binaries to automatically reject accidental `FMA` instructions before packaging.

## Self-Update & Desktop Auto-Updater

- **CLI Self-Update (`anycode update`)**: Added built-in `anycode update` (and `anycode --update` / `-u`) command supporting `--check`, `--version <TAG>`, and `--commit <SHA>` for in-place binary updates across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
- **Desktop Auto-Updater Manifest (`latest.json`)**: Release workflow now enables `createUpdaterArtifacts` when signing keys are configured and publishes `latest.json` across macOS, Linux (`.deb`), and Windows (NSIS).

**Full comparison:** `v0.3.2...v0.3.3`
